[LUNI.8.7.2] **A `::Float` cast strips the dimension.** The dimension of
`x::Float` is none; the result is a bare scalar for every subsequent dimensional
check. This is the author's explicit unit-strip escape hatch already relied on by
[LUNI.8.4]: `let q: Float = r.dist::Float / r.mass::Float` strips both operands to
`Float`, removing the dimensioned × dimensioned ambiguity so the division is a
plain Float operation.
